Patek Philippe · ref. 5811/1G-001

Nautilus

Luxury sports · 37.5–42mm · 60–120m · automatic · 2006–2022

The Patek Philippe Nautilus is a luxury sports watch defined by its porthole-inspired octagonal bezel and integrated bracelet. Originally a bold statement in steel, it has become an icon of elegant and sporty design.

The story

Introduced in 1976 with the Gérald Genta-designed Reference 3700, the Nautilus was Patek Philippe's answer to the burgeoning market for high-end steel sports watches. Initially met with a tepid response due to its large size and steel construction at a luxury price point, the family expanded in 1981 with the smaller Ref. 3800, which introduced an in-house movement and broadened its appeal. The collection evolved over the decades, with the 30th-anniversary Ref. 5711 in 2006 becoming a modern phenomenon and defining the family for a new generation. The family has seen a transition from two-part to three-part cases and back again, along with significant caliber updates, cementing its status as a pillar of watch design.

References by era

3700/1A1976–1990
The original 'Jumbo' in steel, with a 42mm two-part case and no seconds hand.
3800/1A1981–2006
A mid-size 37.5mm version that introduced an in-house caliber and a central seconds hand.
3712/1A2005–2006
A short-lived reference that first introduced the asymmetrical moonphase and power reserve display.
5711/1A2006–2021
The modern successor to the 3700, with a 40mm three-part case and sapphire caseback. Includes sub-references like the blue dial 5711/1A-010 and the final olive green dial 5711/1A-014.
5712/1A-0012006–present
Successor to the 3712, featuring the signature asymmetrical dial with moonphase, date, and power reserve, housed in the modern 40mm case.
5811/1G-0012022–present
The current-production successor to the 5711, in white gold with a slightly larger 41mm two-part case.
